title: Regional license compatibility & legal-delta matrix + integration planning
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a decision-ready artifact that maps commercial and licensing differences across candidate model providers by region, surfaces legal term deltas that affect customer procurement (SLA, data residency, export controls, indemnity, audit rights), and ties those deltas to estimated integration effort and product/ops guardrails required to support each provider in Redwood Dedicated/Private and Hosted offerings.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical matrix listing 10 prioritized model providers x 6 regions with: license type, data residency constraints, export-control flags, indemnity & warranty notes, audit/KMS requirements
Quantified estimate (T-shirt: S/M/L) of product and engineering integration effort per provider-region (e.g., extra legal review, infra changes, SLA gating)
Risk classification (green/amber/red) with recommended mitigation path and one-line exec summary for sales/commercial teams
Confluence doc and an internal summary slide deck delivered; handoff to Solutions Engineering and Legal with a 30-min walkthrough scheduled
Three sample customer-facing procurement notes for high-risk regions (EU finance, APAC export-sensitive, US federal)
tasks: Inventory candidate models from sourcing and procurement (open & partnered models)
Collect licensing documents and region-specific legal advisories from Legal team
Interview Solutions Engineering and SRE on required infra adaptations for data residency and KMS
Estimate integration work with Eng leads (Dedicated, Private, Hosted) and annotate matrix
Draft mitigation playbook (contract clauses, feature toggles, routing policies)
Produce handoff artifacts and schedule cross-functional review
comments: 2025-01-10 Aisha Kumar: Kickoff — scoped 10 providers, asked Legal for expedited license pulls; prioritized EU and APAC regions per sales requests.
2025-01-16 Liam O'Connor: Eng triage — SRE flagged potential KMS/hsm work for provider X in APAC (estimated 5 dev days). Added as a large integration effort.
2025-01-22 Legal (Marina Soto): Received master license files for 6 providers. Two providers have clauses requiring local logging retention — escalated for compliance mapping.

2025-01-28 Product review: Decided to include export-control flag (yes/no/conditional) and an advisory text for Solutions Engineers. PM requested per-provider one-line customer-facing procurement guidance.
2025-02-02 Draft matrix completed — Circulated to Legal and Sales for sanity check. Sales requested separate column for "sales-handoff messaging" (3-line pitch/objection handling).
2025-02-04 Liam O'Connor: Integrated Eng estimates and redlined legal notes. Scheduling final walkthrough with Legal + Solutions Engineering for 2025-02-07.
estimated_impact: Reduces procurement cycle time for enterprise deals in target regions by providing prescriptive guidance; expected to unlock 2-3 pilot deals within 90 days
notes: Trade-offs considered: deeper legal parsing (clauses parsed to sentence-level) is valuable but out-of-scope for this sprint; instead we capture deltas and flag high-risk clauses for Legal to action. Also considered building product-level feature toggles for region gating — deferred until mitigation patterns repeat for >2 providers.
